The results answer the objective, so I am not proposing a revision. The five spatial domains are stable (least-stable Jaccard 0.84, k not at the edge of the searched range) and spatially coherent (0.64, against 0.28 for clustering a spot's own features alone). Every domain spans all 8 patients. That made all 5 testable for markers on the held-out half of the counts: 699 markers, all of which keep their sign when any one patient is left out, with 1.35× more found by the naive per-spot test. Histology image features predict the domains above chance (balanced accuracy 0.36, 95% CI 0.30–0.42, chance 0.20). The slide effect within patients is weak (batch silhouette ≈0, about 3% of variance between slides of one patient). ComBat raised mixing from 0.32 to 0.71 while keeping 75% of within-slide neighbourhoods. Spatially variable gene calls are well calibrated: 5.5% of permuted genes reach p < 0.05, against an expected 5%. Two criteria fail narrowly. On the fit half, the first principal component still tracks library size (correlation 0.52, threshold 0.5). The 2-D map's trustworthiness is 0.79 (threshold 0.8). The report should flag one caveat: library size still explains much of the top 10 components (R² 0.90 after log normalisation). Some of that may reflect real differences in tissue density rather than technical noise.
